title: Injective module-valued hypercover rows are acyclic over any ring
statement: For a qcqs scheme X, a finite split etale hypercover U [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover], a ring R, and an injective sheaf F of left R-modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions] [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the actual terminal-section augmentation [lem-sc-hypercover-resolution-comparison] from F(X) concentrated in degree zero to the alternating section complex C(U,F) is a quasi-isomorphism. No commutativity, affineness, weak contractibility, nonzero-ring or nonempty-base hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01H0, theorem-cohomology-hypercoverings, first proof using an injective-resolution double complex.

proof.text: Replace the small etale category by ULiftHom to put homs and objects in one small-category universe. Its induced topology is subcanonical, and the topology-generated precoverage gives the same Grothendieck topology. Hypercover matching universal properties turn its surjective etale matching maps into locally solvable lower-simplex lifting families.

Realize F as a module sheaf over the sheafified constant ring. The scalar equivalence leaves the section abelian presheaf unchanged and transports injectivity. Apply arbitrary-ring injective hypercover exactness on the equivalent small site.

Identify the displayed alternating sums with the alternating coface differential. Degree-zero exactness and injectivity prove quasi-isomorphism in degree zero; positive exactness proves all positive cohomology groups vanish.
